t.2.28.1: Then Rāma of great splendor spoke to the heroic Lakṣmaṇa, who stood before him, eager to go on ahead, pleading with hands joined in supplication.
t.2.28.2: O Saumitri, if you go with me today to that forest, who will support Kausalyā or the illustrious Sumitrā?
t.2.28.4: For she, the daughter of King Aśvapati, having obtained this kingdom, will do no good to her grieving co-wives.
t.2.28.3: He who showers people with the objects of their desires, as Parjanya showers the earth with rain, that lord of the earth of great splendour is now entangled in the noose of desire.
t.2.28.5: Thus addressed by Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, skilled in speech, then replied in gentle words to Rāma, who was himself a master of speech.
t.2.28.7: The noble Kausalyā could support even a thousand men like me, she who has obtained as her livelihood the revenue of a thousand villages.
t.2.28.6: By your power alone, O hero, Bharata will dutifully honor both Kausalyā and Sumitrā; of this there is no doubt.
t.2.28.8: Taking up my bow together with its arrows, and carrying a spade and a basket, I shall go ahead of you, showing you the path.
t.2.28.10: You, sir, shall take your delight with Vaidehī upon the slopes of the mountains, while I shall do everything for you, whether you are waking or asleep.
t.2.28.9: I will always bring you roots and fruits of the forest, and whatever other things are the proper food of ascetics.
t.2.28.11: Rāma, greatly pleased by these words, replied to him: "Go, Saumitri, and take leave of all your friends and kinsfolk."
t.2.28.12: And those two divine bows, terrible to behold, which the great-souled Varuṇa himself gave to King Janaka at his great sacrifice.
t.2.28.13: The two divine coats of armour that cannot be pierced, the two quivers with inexhaustible arrows, and both swords, spotless as the sun and adorned with gold.
t.2.28.14: All of this has been reverently placed in the house of our teacher. Take up the weapons, Lakṣmaṇa, and come back quickly.
t.2.28.15: Resolved upon dwelling in the forest, he took leave of his friends and kin; then, having bidden farewell to the preceptor of the Ikṣvākus, he took up his finest weapon.
t.2.28.16: Saumitri, a tiger among princes, showed Rāma all those divine weapons, honoured with worship and adorned with garlands.
t.2.28.17: To Lakṣmaṇa, who had come, the self-possessed Rāma spoke with affection: "You have come at the very time I wished for, gentle Lakṣmaṇa."
t.2.28.18: O scorcher of foes, together with you I wish to give away this wealth of mine to the brāhmaṇas and the ascetics.
t.2.28.19: Here dwell the best of the twice-born, firmly devoted to their gurus; and of them, and further of all those who live in dependence on me…
t.2.28.20: But you, quickly bring here the noble Suyajña, son of Vasiṣṭha, foremost among the twice-born. After honoring him and all the other cultured twice-born, I shall set out for the forest.
